headline: Nvidia ends the Shield TV and raises the Shield TV Pro price by 50%
dek: The company blames industry-wide memory costs, driven by demand for AI components, according to TechRadar and Wired.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The base model is gone, the Pro costs more
body: Nvidia discontinued the standard Shield TV, its streaming device, and raised the Shield TV Pro price from $199 to $299 (TechRadar, Wired). The new price took effect October 2 (Wired).

An Nvidia spokesperson explained: “the cost of components, including memory, has increased substantially across the industry” (Wired). TechRadar attributes the same explanation to the official announcement.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Why an old device gets more expensive
s3.body: Generative AI's demand for chips and memory is raising the price of anything with memory or storage, even with years-old parts (Wired).

points.t: Nvidia builds every Shield it sells and has no stockpile of pre-AI-era parts to cushion the increase (TechRadar).
The Pro still runs a Tegra X1 chip with 3GB of RAM and 16GB of storage, with no refresh in years (TechRadar).
Nvidia itself is among the biggest winners of the GPU market that is pushing component prices higher (TechRadar).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: The AI bill reaches consumers
body: The case shows AI pressure on the price of everyday electronics. According to Wired, in 2026 almost anything with memory or storage is getting more expensive.
Consoles follow the same path: Sony's PS5 Pro launched at $699.99 in 2024 and now costs $899.99. Nintendo, Microsoft and Sony all raised prices in recent months (Wired).

stat.cap: from $199 to $299 for the Shield TV Pro

s5.label: What comes next
s5.title: The slow end of a passion project

items.t: The standard Shield TV vanished from official retail channels, with no sign of restocking (TechRadar).
The Shield TV Pro moves to $299 and the standard model is discontinued (TechRadar, Wired).
Nvidia keeps GeForce Now, cloud gaming on PC, mobile and smart TV, and bets on its RTX Spark chip (TechRadar).

caption.hook: Nvidia discontinued the Shield TV and raised the Shield TV Pro price by 50%, from $199 to $299.
body: Launched in 2019, the Shield TV Pro plays 4K HDR video with Dolby Vision and uses AI to upscale content to 4K at 60 frames per second, according to TechRadar.

Wired recalls that Nvidia executive Andrew Bell once called the Shield a “passion project” inside the company. For the outlet, the device still makes sense mainly for buyers who need its broad codec support or a Plex server. TechRadar adds that a new Apple TV is reportedly expected soon, so shoppers may want to compare first.
